meaning: to carry, to take, to wear
title: Spanish Verb Llevar Practice: Meanings, Conjugation and Quiz
description: Practice the Spanish verb llevar: to carry, to take, to wear and to spend time, present and preterite forms, ten self-correcting questions and a reading.
intro: Llevar is a regular -ar verb with many meanings: to carry, to take someone somewhere, to wear clothes and to have been doing something for a time. Learn each use and practice with questions that explain every answer.

uses.example: Llevo los libros en la mochila.
uses.meaning: I carry my books in my backpack.

uses.use: To take someone or something somewhere
uses.example: Mi papá me lleva a la escuela.
uses.meaning: My dad takes me to school.

uses.example: Hoy llevas una camisa muy bonita.
uses.meaning: You're wearing a very nice shirt today.

uses.example: Llevo dos años en esta ciudad.
uses.meaning: I've been in this city for two years.

uses.example: Me llevo bien con mi hermano.
uses.meaning: I get along well with my brother.

quiz.after: una botella de agua en la mochila.

quiz.why: Time spent doing something: llevar + time.

quiz.after: tamales a la cena de Navidad.

paragraphs: Emilia tiene once años y lleva una mochila enorme a la escuela. Lleva libros, cuadernos, su almuerzo, una botella de agua y, a veces, su flauta para la clase de música. Su mamá dice que lleva la casa entera en la espalda.

Un día, la maestra pesó las mochilas de todos los estudiantes. La de Emilia pesaba siete kilos. La maestra les explicó que una mochila no debe pesar más del diez por ciento de su peso. Desde entonces, Emilia lleva solo lo necesario y deja algunos libros en el casillero.

comprehension.before: Su mamá dice que Emilia lleva
options: la casa entera en la espalda
comprehension.why: The whole house on her back.
She only carries what she needs.

mistakes.wrong: Llevo dos años que vivo aquí.
Traigo a mi hermano a la escuela (from home).
mistakes.right: Llevo a mi hermano a la escuela.
mistakes.why: Llevar is toward a place away from the speaker; traer is toward the speaker.
For clothes, the simple present is more natural.
The preterite yo needs an accent: llevé.

heritage: Many heritage speakers use llevar for wearing and carrying naturally. Watch two things in writing: «llevé» needs an accent, and the llevar/traer distinction, which depends on where the speaker is: «¿Me lo traes?» (bring it here) vs «Te lo llevo» (I'll take it to you).
teacher: Ask students to describe what three classmates are wearing today with lleva, then what they carry in their backpacks.
